title: Frobenius trace series
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$.
A *Frobenius module* is a pair $(V,F)$ consisting of a
finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector space $V$ and a $\Qlb$-linear
automorphism $F:V\to V$, in the sense of the
finite-dimensional
Frobenius-module convention of the framework chapter. For such a pair, define its
*trace series* and its *determinant*

$$
\operatorname{tr}_F(T)
=\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(F^n\mid V)\frac{T^n}{n}
\in T\Qlb[[T]],
\qquad
P_{(V,F)}(T)=\det(1-TF\mid V)\in\Qlb[T].
$$

The polynomial $P_{(V,F)}(T)$ has constant coefficient $1$ and degree
$\dim_{\Qlb}V$ (its leading coefficient is $(-1)^{\dim V}\det F\neq0$).

For a *finite graded family* of Frobenius modules
$(V_i,F_i)_{i\in I}$, indexed by a finite subset $I\subset\mathbf Z$, the
*alternating trace series* of the family is

$$
\operatorname{str}_F(T)
=\sum_{n\geq1}\left(\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^i
\Tr\bigl(F_i^n\mid V_i\bigr)\right)\frac{T^n}{n}
=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}_{F_i}(T)
\in T\Qlb[[T]].
$$

No semisimplicity of $F$ (or of the $F_i$) is assumed anywhere.

In the geometric situation, let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant
Weil sheaf, and let $F$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
on $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ in the geometric-Frobenius
convention; for every $0\leq i\leq2d$ the pair
$(H^i(X,\Qlb),F|_{H^i})$ is a Frobenius module, the trace series of the
pair being the degree-$i$ trace series obtained from the
smooth-proper
cohomological family by scalar extension. For the finite graded family
$(H^i(X,\Qlb),F|_{H^i})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$, with $I=\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, the
alternating trace series above is

$$
\operatorname{str}_F(T)
=\sum_{n\geq1}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i
\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H^i(X,\Qlb)\bigr)\right)\frac{T^n}{n}.
$$

proof.text: Put $L=\Qlb$. Its subfield $\Ql$ has characteristic zero by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], so each positive integer $n$ is nonzero and invertible in $L$. By [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] the numbers $a_n=\Tr(F^n\mid V)/n$ are defined for every $n\geq1$. Define the sequence $a_0=0$, $a_n=\Tr(F^n\mid V)/n$ for $n>0$. This is an element of $L[[T]]$ by [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Its zero constant coefficient means it equals $T\sum_{m\geq0}a_{m+1}T^m$, so it lies in $TL[[T]]$. This constructs the trace series without any convergence condition.

Define $P_{(V,F)}$ as the reverse characteristic polynomial [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial], namely the determinant of $1-TF$ after extension to $L[T]$. Apply [lem-weil-reverse-charpoly-coefficients] over the field $L$ to the finite-dimensional space $V$ and its invertible endomorphism $F$. Its first and third clauses give constant coefficient $1$, degree $\dim_LV$, and leading coefficient $(-1)^{\dim_LV}\det F$. This coefficient is nonzero: a polynomial of that degree has nonzero leading coefficient, including dimension zero, when $P=1$.

source.place: first displayed formula, determinant, and following coefficient/degree sentence

proof.text: For a finite $I\subset\mathbf Z$, define $b_0=0$ and $b_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^i\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i)$ for $n>0$, with $(-1)^i=1$ for even integers and $-1$ for odd integers. These coefficients define a formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series]. The coefficient of $T^n$ in the finite sum $\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}_{F_i}(T)$ is zero for $n=0$, and for $n>0$ is $\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^i(\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i)/n)=b_n$ by finite distributivity. Equality of coefficient sequences proves the two displayed descriptions agree. As in Step 1 the vanishing constant coefficient puts this series in $TL[[T]]$. This works for the empty family and for negative indices.

In the geometric situation, take $E=\Ql$ and the constant Weil sheaf. The hypotheses of [prop-cohomological-finiteness] hold: $X_0$ is proper, hence separated and of finite type, $\ell\ne p$, and the constant Weil sheaf is the indicated coefficient object. It follows that every $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$ is finite-dimensional and its geometric Frobenius $F_{i,\ell}$ is an automorphism. These are exactly the spaces and operators used to define the family in [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]; this definition itself is not used as a finiteness theorem.

Apply [lem-weil-cohomology-scalar-extension-qlbar] with the same smooth, proper, geometrically connected $X_0$ of pure dimension $d$. It identifies $V_{i,\ell}\otimes_{\Ql}L$ with $H^i(X,L)$ and intertwines $F_{i,\ell}\otimes1$ with the global geometric Frobenius on the latter. Extend a finite basis of $V_{i,\ell}$ to $L$ and transport it by this identification. In this basis the Frobenius matrix is the coefficientwise image of its $\Ql$-matrix $A_i$; its inverse is the image of $A_i^{-1}$, so it is an automorphism and the space remains finite-dimensional. For each $n\geq1$, matrix multiplication gives the image of $A_i^n$ as its $n$th power. The trace is the sum of diagonal entries [def-weil-endomorphism-trace], so its trace is the image of $\Tr(A_i^n)$, and division by the nonzero integer $n$ commutes with the field embedding. Thus each degree-$i$ trace series is precisely coefficientwise scalar extension of the one for the smooth-proper family. Finally $I=\{0,\ldots,2d\}$ is finite, so substitution of these Frobenius modules into Step 3 gives the last displayed alternating series. No diagonalization or semisimplicity was used.
